title: Spending tokens without regretting it
target: How to approach the cosmetic machine in R.E.P.O. so a token is a decision rather than a reflex.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with the cosmetic machine in it
A rough idea of which part of your avatar you want to change

steps.do: Treat the machine as a dispenser with a sequence rather than as a shelf.
steps.because: it is run by an animator that points back at the machine, so what it does is a sequence with a beginning and a payoff (CosmeticShopMachine, CosmeticShopMachineAnimator)

steps.do: Expect a token at one of four grades rather than a named item.
steps.because: the game keeps cosmetic tokens in four grades, each with its own colouring (CosmeticShopToken_Basecolor_Common, CosmeticShopToken_Basecolor_Uncommon, CosmeticShopToken_Basecolor_Rare, CosmeticShopToken_Basecolor_UltraRare)

steps.do: Judge the pull after the display has come to rest, not while it is spinning.
steps.because: the screen spins and then settles on a separate transform with its own curve (screenSpinTransform, screenSpinSettleTransform)

steps.do: Look at what you already own before spending again.
steps.because: a cosmetic can be hidden again rather than only collected, so owning one is not the same as wearing it (CosmeticHideCondition)

steps.do: Check which part of the avatar the cosmetic lands on.
steps.because: the avatar is split into parts such as the head, the body, an arm and a leg, each carrying a default surface (Cosmetic - Head Top Mesh - Default, Cosmetic - Body Top Mesh - Default)

steps.do: Pick cosmetic objects up from the floor through their own interface.
steps.because: cosmetic objects in the world have an interface of their own, and tokens have one as well (CosmeticWorldObjectUI, CosmeticTokenUI)

commonMistakes: Spending for a named cosmetic when the machine hands over a token at a grade.
Judging a pull before the display has settled.
Buying a second copy of something you already own and have only hidden.
Forgetting that a cosmetic is laid over one part of the avatar rather than the whole figure.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
